items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: We made this Rag-and-Roll Revue. She named it the Rag-and-Roll Revue, but she... She featured me a whole lot, you know.

ctx.x: going to do, you know... So we got together and had a rehearsal at some studio she rented out. She rented a studio on 45th Street and Eighth Avenue. We had a rehearsal two or three times.

We made this Rag-and-Roll Revue. She named it the Rag-and-Roll Revue, but she... She featured me a whole lot, you know. And in fact, we... We didn't record it, but we were working on stage, we worked together. We'd do things like, oh, let's see... "Jelly-Roll"... Like, "I ain't gonna do ...(?)... my jelly-roll" just by myself. And what else ....(?). Oh, "All Of Me." But anyway, she was doing things where we worked together. She'd sing one chorus of it and I'd sing the second chorus, then I'd sing the third…

In other words, she is a stylist who, even though she is a young woman, in her early thirties now, and at the time, in '76 or '78, she was singing music hearkening back to the 1920's, and she admires Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey and early Victoria Spivey and Ida Cox and those people...
